chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from a number of our companions from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no cutting (amputation of the hand) upon the one who embezzles, and there is no cutting upon the one who displaces the dirhams from the cloth of the man.

key_terms.قَطْعٌ: Cutting (amputation of the hand as a hadd punishment)
key_terms.يَسْتَلِبُ: Embezzles or takes possession of property

ai.seo_question: When is the punishment of cutting the hand not obligatory for theft in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the hadd punishment of amputation is not obligatory for the embezzler (mustalib) or for one who removes coins from a garment, distinguishing these cases from the strict conditions of theft (sariqa) where the item is taken from its secure place (mihfaz). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise definition of 'taking' and the security of the stored item, ensuring the hadd is applied only when all legal criteria are fully met.
